solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Lying about source of money pocketed by copper (corrupt)

parts.note: re is the Latin-derived word for 'concerning', a common crossword sense of about
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

indicators.note: the source of a word is its opening letter, here of money

parts.note: bent is slang for dishonest or corrupt

explanation.surface: A crooked police officer pockets cash and lies about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' looks like a policeman but gives the chemical symbol CU, which holds M from 'source of money'.
explanation.definitionFit: Recumbent is a formal adjective for reclining or lying down, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Survey's right with European community committee disheartened

parts.note: C is a common abbreviation for community

indicators.note: a word losing its heart keeps only its outside letters, here of committee

explanation.surface: A survey is said to be right, backed by a European Community committee that has lost its spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after Survey stands for 'is', a link to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A recce is informal military shorthand for a reconnaissance, a scouting survey of ground.

clue.text: Very well, to make matters worse, they finished

parts.note: the idiom 'to cap it all' means to make matters worse still

indicators.note: the finish of a word is its final letter, here of they

explanation.surface: Things were going very well until, to make matters worse, they finished.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase 'to make matters worse' is the idiom 'to cap it all', giving CAP IT ALL, and 'they finished' gives its last letter Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Capitally is a dated British adverb meaning excellently, in a first-rate manner.

clue.text: Ducks answer welcomed by unions

indicators.note: being welcomed by something puts one piece inside the other

parts.note: mergers are unions of companies

explanation.surface: Trade unions welcome a reply — or ducks one.
explanation.definitionFit: Mergansers are fish-eating diving ducks with saw-edged bills, so the definition is by class.

clue.text: Went out across cape, emotionally charged

indicators.note: one piece lying across another surrounds it here

parts.note: exited means left or went out
C is the map abbreviation for cape

explanation.surface: Someone went out over a headland in an emotional state.
explanation.definitionFit: Excited describes being stirred up or worked up, a feeling of emotional charge.

clue.text: Get rid of grass (unfashionable)

parts.note: turf is grass with its roots and soil
out means no longer in fashion

explanation.surface: Remove grass that is no longer in style.
explanation.definitionFit: To turf out is a British idiom for ejecting or evicting someone, so to get rid of them.

clue.text: Bound to miss the end of autumn shoot

indicators.note: missing a letter means dropping it from the word

parts.note: a spring is a bound or leap

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter, here of autumn

explanation.surface: A leap that misses autumn's end, as if a season were skipped.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprig is a small stem or shoot cut from a plant.

clue.text: Hide, if virtually broke

indicators.note: virtually means almost, so the word stops just short of its last letter

parts.note: skint is British slang for having no money

explanation.surface: Go into hiding if you are almost out of money.
explanation.walkthrough: SKINT is everyday British slang for broke.
explanation.definitionFit: A hide is an animal's skin, the noun sense of the clue word.

clue.text: Settle origins of riots over open season thus

indicators.note: the origins of words are their opening letters, taken from each of the next five words

explanation.surface: Calm things down once riots begin over the start of the hunting season.
explanation.definitionFit: To roost is to settle for rest, as birds do on a perch.

clue.text: Ensure sentry finishes early, with ease, say, to support worker

indicators.note: in a down entry the supporting piece sits below the one it holds up
stopping early loses the final letter

parts.note: a guard is a sentry
ant is the standard crossword worker, from worker ants

indicators.note: say signals that we go by how the word is spoken

parts.note: the word ease is spoken like the plural of the letter E

explanation.surface: A guard leaves early and easily, to back up a labourer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ease, say' sounds like 'E's', two Es, which sit beneath ANT in this down light.
explanation.definitionFit: To guarantee something is to make certain of it, a straight synonym of ensure.

clue.text: Primate caught in credit scam

indicators.note: caught in puts one piece inside another

parts.note: CR is the accounting abbreviation for credit
an ape is a primate

explanation.surface: A monkey is caught up in a credit fraud.
explanation.definitionFit: A caper is informal for a criminal scheme or escapade, close to a scam.

clue.text: In the circus, mostly finding enlisted men and beasts

indicators.note: enlisted means taken in, so one piece is set inside the other
mostly means all but the last letter

parts.note: a carnival is a travelling fair or circus
OR, other ranks, is the military term for enlisted men

explanation.surface: At the circus, soldiers and animals are found together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Enlisted men' reads as one phrase but 'enlisted' is the signal to put OR inside CARNIVA.
explanation.definitionFit: Carnivora is the zoological order of flesh-eating mammals, so a group of beasts.

clue.text: Removal of family history?

definitions.meaning: taking something out, like a tooth at the dentist
one's descent or ancestry, as in 'of Irish descent'

explanation.surface: A puzzled question whether removing something counts as family history.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both pulling out and lineage or origin, as in 'of Italian ancestry'.

clue.text: Sort of colonnade to put in South America

indicators.note: put in places one piece inside another

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An architect plans to build a colonnade in South America.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoa is a classical Greek covered walkway or portico, a kind of colonnade.

clue.text: Caught line in wild oriental grass

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: in puts one piece inside another
wild means unruly, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A line catches some wild oriental grass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' puts L into ORIENTAL before 'wild' scrambles the result into ITRONELLA.
explanation.definitionFit: Citronella is a fragrant South Asian grass whose oil repels insects.

clue.text: Exploited laid-up press chief, employing American

parts.note: someone laid up is ill in bed
ed, short for editor, is the chief of a newspaper

explanation.surface: A sick newspaper editor felt exploited when hiring an American.
explanation.definitionFit: Ill-used means treated badly or taken advantage of.

clue.text: Popular autocrat has no time initially for signal

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular

indicators.note: has no signals a letter being dropped
initially says it is the first of the two time letters that goes

parts.note: a dictator is an autocrat

explanation.surface: A well-liked autocrat runs out of time at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping the first T of DICTATOR leaves DICATOR.
explanation.definitionFit: An indicator is a gauge or pointer that gives a signal or sign.

clue.text: One in three rent after fall

indicators.note: after puts the rent piece behind the fall piece

parts.note: a trip is a stumble or fall
to let is to rent out

explanation.surface: One of three tenants pays rent after a tumble.
explanation.definitionFit: A triplet is one of three children born at one birth.

clue.text: Waste water, say on brewing tea

parts.note: water is an example of a liquid

indicators.note: brewing means stewing or fermenting, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: Waste water, perhaps from making tea.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down light 'on' puts the first piece above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: Liquidate is slang for kill or wipe out, as is the American slang sense of waste.

clue.text: An excursion that provides pay dirt, possibly

indicators.note: possibly signals one of several possible arrangements of the letters

explanation.surface: A prospecting outing that strikes paying ore.
explanation.definitionFit: A short outing done in a single daylight span is an excursion.

clue.text: How one may be sent off for boxing?

definitions.text: How one may be sent off
definitions.meaning: the idiom 'send someone ...' means dismiss them abruptly
putting goods into boxes or cases

explanation.walkthrough: 'Boxing' looks like the sport, which would send a fighter off, but it means putting things in boxes.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both the curt dismissal in 'sent packing' and stowing items in crates.

clue.text: Annoyance felt inhaling the Queen's tobacco

indicators.note: inhaling takes something in, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: pique is a feeling of irritation
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: Irritation as someone breathes in the monarch's tobacco smoke.
explanation.definitionFit: Perique is a strong dark tobacco grown in Louisiana, used in pipe blends.

clue.text: Stick out for a planned undertaking

definitions.meaning: a scheme or venture worked out in advance

explanation.surface: Persist with a venture you had planned.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb the word means jut, as a noun a scheme of work.

clue.text: Source of cheap green crop

indicators.note: the source of a word is its first letter, here of cheap

parts.note: green means raw or inexperienced

explanation.surface: A farmer explains where an unripe harvest came cheaply.
explanation.definitionFit: A bird's crop is its craw, the pouch in the gullet where food is stored.

clue.text: White drops the last two for a record

indicators.note: the final pair of letters are cut off

parts.note: albumen is the white of an egg

explanation.surface: A white album that lost its final two tracks.
explanation.definitionFit: An album is a long-playing record or collection of tracks.

clue.text: Finance bill having an effect

parts.note: AC, short for account, is a bill
counting means mattering or having weight

explanation.surface: A finance bill that is starting to make an impact.
explanation.definitionFit: Accounting is the recording and management of money, a branch of finance.

clue.text: Good boy given new organ

indicators.note: given here means handed something to hold, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: A well-behaved boy receives a new organ, as in a transplant.
explanation.definitionFit: A gland is a body organ that secretes substances such as hormones.

clue.text: Nothing more than water

definitions.meaning: a lake or pond, as in English place names

explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means only or simple; the noun is an old word for a lake.

clue.text: Board victory — start to expect drink!

parts.note: board and table both mean food served, or a flat surface
a win is a victory

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter, here of expect

explanation.surface: A boardroom victory — expect drinks all round!
explanation.definitionFit: Table wine is ordinary wine served with meals, a drink.

clue.text: Team allowed to restrain such a creature

indicators.note: restrain read as 'hold back' signals the held letters run backwards
to here is taken as within, holding letters of the next words

explanation.surface: A team is allowed to keep an animal on a lead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To restrain' is read as 'hold back': the letters held inside 'Team allowed', read backwards, give the creature.
explanation.definitionFit: The definition points back to the creature held in the clue, a South American camelid.

clue.text: Grass that is given to sheep

indicators.note: given to says the 'that is' piece is attached after the sheep

parts.note: a ram is a male sheep
ie, id est, means that is

explanation.surface: Grass that is fed to sheep.
explanation.definitionFit: Ramie is an Asian nettle-family plant grown for fibre, loosely called a grass.

clue.text: Understands a boss's advances

parts.note: gets means understands, as in 'I get it'
a head is a boss, the possessive adds no letter

explanation.surface: Someone who understands the boss's ideas moves up.
explanation.definitionFit: To get ahead is to progress or make advances in a career.
